summary: Build practical irrigation management and water-efficient agriculture skills in 5 days. Learn to design, schedule, and optimize farm water use.
lede: Irrigation management connects crop water demand, soil conditions and system performance to practical water-use decisions. For farm and project professionals, this training addresses how to plan, operate and improve irrigation under changing field and water conditions. Participants learn to calculate crop water needs, design or adjust drip and sprinkler systems, and schedule and monitor irrigation using soil moisture, climate and system-performance data.
audienceIntro: This irrigation management and water-efficient agriculture course is tailored for professionals responsible for planning, operating, and optimizing farm and project-level water use.
modules: Irrigation Management Foundations and Climate Context
Calculating Crop Water Requirements and Irrigation Needs
Designing and Adjusting Drip and Sprinkler Systems
Irrigation Scheduling and On-Farm Water Management
Monitoring System Performance and Troubleshooting Issues
Water-Efficient Agriculture Practices and Soil Moisture Conservation
Digital Tools, Sensors, and Precision Irrigation Concepts
Water Governance, Compliance, and Collective Irrigation Management
Integrating an Irrigation Management Plan and Reporting
prerequisites: This intermediate course assumes you already have basic familiarity with crop production and general irrigation concepts. You should understand fundamental agronomy (crop growth stages, basic soil types), have experience working with at least one irrigation method in practice, and be comfortable using spreadsheets for simple calculations. No coding or specialized software skills are required, but you should bring a laptop for scheduling, calculations, and simple data analysis. Advanced topics such as precision irrigation, remote sensing, and IoT-based control are covered at conceptual and operational application levels rather than full engineering design depth.
